findings.title: Change folder… still refuses a pendingInit workspace's moved folder when it holds another id's identity
findings.body: The pendingInit fix at line 848 covers a moved folder with no identity. The earlier thread also named a second case, and it is still refused. A `pendingInit` entry has a minted id. Suppose its folder is remounted elsewhere and already holds an identity.json with a different id, for example one written by another Mac. `checkRelocate` returns `different` at lines 836-838. `availability` adopts that id at lines 711-721 (`entry.pendingInit && !this.get(identity.identity.id)`). So the user is told the folder holds a different workspace and cannot repoint it, although a probe would have accepted it. Applying the same adoption rule in `checkRelocate` (accept when `entry.pendingInit && !this.get(identity.identity.id)`) would close it. `relocate` would then need the probe to run afterwards so the id is adopted, which `relocateFolder` already does at `index.ts:342`.

findings.title: An offline edit of only the name turns the cached upgrade color into a pendingIdentity write, overwriting another Mac's recolor
findings.body: The `edit` update callback deletes `pendingColorUpgrade` and sets `pendingIdentity = true` (lines 629-631). When the folder is back, the `pendingIdentity` branch (lines 663-672) writes the cached name, color and initials over the folder's file without comparing. Take the migrated Default with a cached color of `kaipu` and a not-connected folder. The user renames it offline, which changes the name only. Meanwhile another Mac recolors that folder's file to `sky`. When the folder returns, its file is overwritten with `kaipu`, a color this user never chose (it came from the deferred upgrade). The other Mac's recolor is lost with no visible sign. The new test at `registry-create-edit.test.ts:206` pins this outcome for an unchanged folder, but nothing covers the case where the folder changed meanwhile. `pendingIdentity` already overwrites whole cached fields for any offline edit, so this follows the existing design. The upgrade makes it more likely, because the user did not set the color. One option is to drop `pendingColorUpgrade` only when the edit changes the color, and let the name-only edit keep the cached color behind the old-Default check.

contracts.action: Deferred brand-color upgrade now has its own marker `pendingColorUpgrade`, applied by `availability` only when the folder's file is still the old Default in rose
contracts.equivalent_path: The `pendingIdentity` branch at registry.ts:663-680, which writes the cached identity over the folder's file without comparing.
contracts.before_after: Before: the upgrade reused `pendingIdentity`, so the cached color overwrote whatever the folder held. After: the file is rewritten only if `isOldDefault`; otherwise the stale-cache path at 691-708 adopts the folder's identity and drops the marker. An edit, the `pendingIdentity` write and the no-identity rewrite all clear the marker (lines 629, 674, 740). The no-op edit's `savedToFolder` also accounts for it (585-586).
contracts.visible_effect: The Default workspace shows its brand color from the cache at once. The folder's file catches up on reconnect, or this Mac adopts the other Mac's rename or recolor.
contracts.failure_mode: Overlap: `availability` reads the identity at 657, awaits, then writes at 684 from that earlier read. A concurrent `edit` that writes between those two points would have its name replaced by the stale one. `pendingIdentity` has the same window and the `update` lock does not cover these file writes. The window is narrow, because `edit` probes first, which clears the marker. A write failure keeps the marker, so the next probe retries.

contracts.action: Change folder… accepts a folder with `.kaipu` and no identity when the entry is pendingInit
contracts.equivalent_path: `availability` for an entry with no identity file (registry.ts:724-747), which writes the identity under the registered id.
contracts.before_after: Before: `has-items-no-identity` for any folder with `.kaipu` and no identity. After: accepted for pendingInit entries. `relocateFolder` then calls `reg.availability` (index.ts:342), which writes the identity under the registered id and clears `pendingInit`.
contracts.visible_effect: The moved folder of a workspace registered while its drive was away can now be repointed. The foreign-identity case is still refused.
contracts.failure_mode: `registry.relocate` runs `checkRelocate` again, so the rule holds on the direct call too. A failed identity write at `availability` leaves `pendingInit` set and retries on the next probe.

contracts.action: Picking the workspace's current folder returns early in `relocateWorkspace`, before any window is asked to prepare
contracts.equivalent_path: The not-active path (`registry.relocate`) and `relocateActive` (the switch transaction), which prompt windows, bump the generation and drop pending captures.
contracts.before_after: Before: the full transaction ran for a no-op. After: `checkRelocate` still validates, then `resolve()` equality returns the current entry. The caller still probes (index.ts:342), broadcasts and refreshes titles, so an identity file deleted by hand is rewritten.
contracts.visible_effect: No save prompt, no route remount and no dropped capture when the user re-picks the same folder. The toast still says "Done".
contracts.failure_mode: Comparison is by `resolve`, so a case-only or symlink difference on macOS takes the full transaction, which is harmless.

contracts.action: Rejected create, edit and relocate IPC calls are caught and shown as an 'uncertain' message in the dialog, and as a toast from Settings
contracts.equivalent_path: The refusal path (`setRefusal(result.reason)`, `setFolderError`) for resolved refusals, and `remove` in workspaces-context.tsx:193, which does not catch.
contracts.before_after: Before: a rejection left `busy` cleared by `finally` but showed nothing, and the Settings click did nothing. After: `catch` sets `create-uncertain`, `edit-uncertain` or `relocateUncertain`, and the context shows a toast. Typing in the name field clears the refusal (line 191).
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees that the result is unknown and is told to check before retrying. A create that actually registered the workspace will have arrived by the `workspaces:changed` broadcast.
contracts.failure_mode: The `try` also wraps `onCreated` and `onSaved`; if one threw, a success would show as 'uncertain'. Those callbacks only call setDialog and showToast, so this is theoretical. `remove` still has no catch, which is out of scope for this diff.

thread_replies.reply: The no-identity case is fixed: a `pendingInit` entry now accepts a moved folder with `.kaipu` and no identity (`registry.ts:848`), and a test covers it. The second case from the thread is still refused. A moved folder holding an identity with another id, which `availability` would adopt (`registry.ts:711-721`), still gets `different` at `registry.ts:836-838`. Please apply the same adoption rule there, or tell us it is out of scope.

This PR does not change `switch-transaction.ts`. `relocateActive` still calls `dropPendingCaptures()` when the active workspace is relocated to a different folder. If you want to keep dropping the capture there, a line in the code saying why would help; otherwise it still loses an unsaved screenshot.

Fixed. `relocateWorkspace` now returns the current entry right after `checkRelocate` when the picked folder resolves to the entry's own path (`relocate.ts:42-43`). That skips the prepare prompt, the generation bump and the capture drop. A test covers it (`relocate.test.ts:152`).
Fixed. The "Move to" sentence is removed from `relocateNotWorkspace` in en.json and es.json. The dialog test now asserts that the text is absent.

Fixed. The dialog catches a rejected relocate and shows `relocateUncertain` (`workspace-dialog.tsx:147-149`). The Settings path shows the same message as a toast (`workspaces-context.tsx:177-181`). Both say the result is unknown instead of 'failed', which fits a rejection after main may have applied the change. Tests cover the dialog path.
Fixed. The test now relocates, checks Save is still disabled, then picks a color and checks Save becomes enabled.

input.summary: The part is mostly sound. The new `pendingColorUpgrade` marker, the same-folder early return, the `pendingInit` relocate rule and the rejected-call handling in the dialog and Settings all do what they claim, and the tests match their names. Two minor findings, both "consider". First, relocate for a `pendingInit` workspace still refuses a moved folder that holds another id's identity, although `availability` would adopt it. Second, an offline name-only edit drops the deferred upgrade and later overwrites the folder's color with the cached `kaipu`, which would erase another Mac's recolor. Of the earlier threads, the same-folder, \"Move to\", rejected-relocate and Save-test ones are addressed. The `pendingInit` thread is half addressed, and the `dropPendingCaptures` one is unchanged, since `switch-transaction.ts` is not in this part.

contracts.failure_mode: `registry.relocate` runs `checkRelocate` again, so the rule holds on the direct call too. A failed identity write at `availability` leaves `pendingInit` set and retries on the next probe.

contracts.action: Picking the workspace's current folder returns early in `relocateWorkspace`, before any window is asked to prepare
contracts.equivalent_path: The not-active path (`registry.relocate`) and `relocateActive` (the switch transaction), which prompt windows, bump the generation and drop pending captures.
contracts.before_after: Before: the full transaction ran for a no-op. After: `checkRelocate` still validates, then `resolve()` equality returns the current entry. The caller still probes (index.ts:342), broadcasts and refreshes titles, so an identity file deleted by hand is rewritten.
contracts.visible_effect: No save prompt, no route remount and no dropped capture when the user re-picks the same folder. The toast still says "Done".
contracts.failure_mode: Comparison is by `resolve`, so a case-only or symlink difference on macOS takes the full transaction, which is harmless.

contracts.action: Rejected create, edit and relocate IPC calls are caught and shown as an 'uncertain' message in the dialog, and as a toast from Settings
contracts.equivalent_path: The refusal path (`setRefusal(result.reason)`, `setFolderError`) for resolved refusals, and `remove` in workspaces-context.tsx:193, which does not catch.
contracts.before_after: Before: a rejection left `busy` cleared by `finally` but showed nothing, and the Settings click did nothing. After: `catch` sets `create-uncertain`, `edit-uncertain` or `relocateUncertain`, and the context shows a toast. Typing in the name field clears the refusal (line 191).
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees that the result is unknown and is told to check before retrying. A create that actually registered the workspace will have arrived by the `workspaces:changed` broadcast.
contracts.failure_mode: The `try` also wraps `onCreated` and `onSaved`; if one threw, a success would show as 'uncertain'. Those callbacks only call setDialog and showToast, so this is theoretical. `remove` still has no catch, which is out of scope for this diff.

thread_replies.reply: The no-identity case is fixed: a `pendingInit` entry now accepts a moved folder with `.kaipu` and no identity (`registry.ts:848`), and a test covers it. The second case from the thread is still refused. A moved folder holding an identity with another id, which `availability` would adopt (`registry.ts:711-721`), still gets `different` at `registry.ts:836-838`. Please apply the same adoption rule there, or tell us it is out of scope.

This PR does not change `switch-transaction.ts`. `relocateActive` still calls `dropPendingCaptures()` when the active workspace is relocated to a different folder. If you want to keep dropping the capture there, a line in the code saying why would help; otherwise it still loses an unsaved screenshot.

Fixed. `relocateWorkspace` now returns the current entry right after `checkRelocate` when the picked folder resolves to the entry's own path (`relocate.ts:42-43`). That skips the prepare prompt, the generation bump and the capture drop. A test covers it (`relocate.test.ts:152`).
Fixed. The "Move to" sentence is removed from `relocateNotWorkspace` in en.json and es.json. The dialog test now asserts that the text is absent.

Fixed. The dialog catches a rejected relocate and shows `relocateUncertain` (`workspace-dialog.tsx:147-149`). The Settings path shows the same message as a toast (`workspaces-context.tsx:177-181`). Both say the result is unknown instead of 'failed', which fits a rejection after main may have applied the change. Tests cover the dialog path.
Fixed. The test now relocates, checks Save is still disabled, then picks a color and checks Save becomes enabled.

toolu_01BqCo496VehQG45sv1MSa7s.summary: The part is mostly sound. The new `pendingColorUpgrade` marker, the same-folder early return, the `pendingInit` relocate rule and the rejected-call handling in the dialog and Settings all do what they claim, and the tests match their names. Two minor findings, both "consider". First, relocate for a `pendingInit` workspace still refuses a moved folder that holds another id's identity, although `availability` would adopt it. Second, an offline name-only edit drops the deferred upgrade and later overwrites the folder's color with the cached `kaipu`, which would erase another Mac's recolor. Of the earlier threads, the same-folder, \"Move to\", rejected-relocate and Save-test ones are addressed. The `pendingInit` thread is half addressed, and the `dropPendingCaptures` one is unchanged, since `switch-transaction.ts` is not in this part.

findings.title: Change folder… still refuses a pendingInit workspace's moved folder when it holds another id's identity
findings.body: The pendingInit fix at line 848 covers a moved folder with no identity. The earlier thread also named a second case, and it is still refused. A `pendingInit` entry has a minted id. Suppose its folder is remounted elsewhere and already holds an identity.json with a different id, for example one written by another Mac. `checkRelocate` returns `different` at lines 836-838. `availability` adopts that id at lines 711-721 (`entry.pendingInit && !this.get(identity.identity.id)`). So the user is told the folder holds a different workspace and cannot repoint it, although a probe would have accepted it. Applying the same adoption rule in `checkRelocate` (accept when `entry.pendingInit && !this.get(identity.identity.id)`) would close it. `relocate` would then need the probe to run afterwards so the id is adopted, which `relocateFolder` already does at `index.ts:342`.

findings.title: An offline edit of only the name turns the cached upgrade color into a pendingIdentity write, overwriting another Mac's recolor
findings.body: The `edit` update callback deletes `pendingColorUpgrade` and sets `pendingIdentity = true` (lines 629-631). When the folder is back, the `pendingIdentity` branch (lines 663-672) writes the cached name, color and initials over the folder's file without comparing. Take the migrated Default with a cached color of `kaipu` and a not-connected folder. The user renames it offline, which changes the name only. Meanwhile another Mac recolors that folder's file to `sky`. When the folder returns, its file is overwritten with `kaipu`, a color this user never chose (it came from the deferred upgrade). The other Mac's recolor is lost with no visible sign. The new test at `registry-create-edit.test.ts:206` pins this outcome for an unchanged folder, but nothing covers the case where the folder changed meanwhile. `pendingIdentity` already overwrites whole cached fields for any offline edit, so this follows the existing design. The upgrade makes it more likely, because the user did not set the color. One option is to drop `pendingColorUpgrade` only when the edit changes the color, and let the name-only edit keep the cached color behind the old-Default check.

contracts.action: Deferred brand-color upgrade now has its own marker `pendingColorUpgrade`, applied by `availability` only when the folder's file is still the old Default in rose
contracts.equivalent_path: The `pendingIdentity` branch at registry.ts:663-680, which writes the cached identity over the folder's file without comparing.
contracts.before_after: Before: the upgrade reused `pendingIdentity`, so the cached color overwrote whatever the folder held. After: the file is rewritten only if `isOldDefault`; otherwise the stale-cache path at 691-708 adopts the folder's identity and drops the marker. An edit, the `pendingIdentity` write and the no-identity rewrite all clear the marker (lines 629, 674, 740). The no-op edit's `savedToFolder` also accounts for it (585-586).
contracts.visible_effect: The Default workspace shows its brand color from the cache at once. The folder's file catches up on reconnect, or this Mac adopts the other Mac's rename or recolor.
contracts.failure_mode: Overlap: `availability` reads the identity at 657, awaits, then writes at 684 from that earlier read. A concurrent `edit` that writes between those two points would have its name replaced by the stale one. `pendingIdentity` has the same window and the `update` lock does not cover these file writes. The window is narrow, because `edit` probes first, which clears the marker. A write failure keeps the marker, so the next probe retries.
